newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Shell confirms cut in Japan steam coal price.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Shell confirms cut in Japan steam coal price.

text.p: Shell Australia Ltd on Friday confirmed that thermal coal prices for sales to Japan would be cut by US$2.65 a tonne to US$37.65 a tonne in the 1997/98 fiscal year starting April 1.

Shell said it, Ulan Coal Mines Ltd, MIM Holdings Ltd and South Blackwater Coal, owned by QCT Resources Ltd, had reached an agreement with Chubu Electric Power Co setting the coal price for power generation in Japan.
Ulan is a partnership of Exxon Coal Australia, a subsidiary of Exxon Corp, and Mitsubishi Development Pty Ltd, a unit of Japan's Mitsubishi Corp.
Shell manages four mines in New South Wales and Queensland states, producing thermal (steaming) and metallurgical coals, which are used in steelmaking.
The settlement represented a reasonable outcome under the current difficult circumstances, Shell said.
"When taken together together with the soft prices that sellers are accepting on the spot market, it is clear that the coming year will continue to challenge Australian coal producers," Shell said.
